## The framing

AI is compressing the full-stack product builder's skill set, Strategy, Design & Engineering, Go-to-Market, Data Science, into something one person can wield. The 80/20 reality: AI now does roughly 80% of the technical execution, which makes the remaining 20%, judgment about what to build and whether it's right, the scarce skill. Today you'll feel exactly where that line sits.

## What you'll build: Research Scout

A live literature-scanner web app on the [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org) API, a tool that actually does research work, not just organizes it. Type a research topic → the app queries api.openalex.org live (free, no auth key needed) → matching papers with authors, venue, year, citation count, and DOI → a publication-trend chart by year → save papers to a shortlist → export BibTeX.

Here's the meta-loop: to prepare this workshop, we used AI to scan OpenAlex for what you all are publishing on AI and work. In 55 minutes you'll build your own version of that scanner, and in the debrief we'll use your apps live to test whether the research questions the room proposes are open or crowded. The product you build becomes an instrument in the session itself. And it's a keeper: literature discovery plus "is this space hot?" evidence for your next paper's introduction.

Everyone starts from the same prompt. Sixty people will end with sixty different products, that divergence is data, and we'll talk about it.
